name: Stationary Rotational Medicine Ball Throw
definition: A unilateral two-hand rotational power throw from a fixed split stance, parallel standing stance, or tall-kneeling support. The athlete winds up away from a medicine-ball-safe target and completes one counted repetition with one release toward it, then retrieves or receives the ball and resets. Half-kneeling reactive returns, locomotor approaches, floor slams, chest passes, retained-ball twists, and one-hand shot-put throws remain outside this family.

variantAxes.description: The exact floor contacts retained through the repetition.
The safe receiving environment for the released ball.
Whether an external guide constrains the ball.

exerciseRules.description: The split-stance record retains a fixed forward split support.
The standing record retains a parallel two-foot support.
The tall-kneeling record retains both knees and shins on the floor.

execution.startingPosition: Stand side-on to a medicine-ball-safe wall, prepared partner, or clear throwing area in a comfortable forward split stance with soft knees and the ball in both hands near the hip away from the target.
execution.movement: Keep the chosen split stance, turn the hips and torso away to load the ball, then reverse forcefully and release it once toward the target.
execution.endpoint: One repetition ends when the ball leaves both hands toward the target.
execution.returnPhase: Retrieve the ball or receive it after the repetition, then rebuild the same split stance before the next throw.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep both knees aligned with the feet and do not step during the counted throw.
execution.supportAndPosture: Use a stance you can hold without wobbling and keep the travel and landing area clear.
disqualifyingCompensations: Stepping during the repetition changes it into an approach throw.
Dropping the rear knee changes the support to half-kneeling.
Slamming into the floor changes the target and family.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete the set toward one side, then mirror the stance and perform equal repetitions in the other direction.

execution.startingPosition: Stand side-on to a medicine-ball-safe wall, prepared partner, or clear throwing area with parallel feet about hip-width, soft knees, and the ball in both hands near the hip away from the target.
execution.movement: Turn the hips and torso away to load the ball, reverse forcefully through the feet and trunk, and release it once toward the target.
execution.endpoint: One repetition ends when the ball leaves both hands toward the target.
execution.returnPhase: Retrieve the ball or receive it after the repetition, then reset the same parallel stance before the next throw.
execution.controlledJoints: Keep the knees tracking with the feet and turn through the feet and hips instead of twisting through fixed knees.
execution.supportAndPosture: Maintain balance through the release and keep the receiving area clear.
disqualifyingCompensations: Stepping toward the target changes it into an approach throw.
Using a split stance changes the reviewed support.
Slamming into the floor changes the target and family.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete the set toward one side, then turn around and perform equal repetitions in the other direction.

execution.startingPosition: Kneel tall on both knees and shins, side-on to a prepared partner or clear throwing area, with the ball in both hands near the hip away from the target.
execution.movement: Keep the hips extended, turn the torso and ball away, then reverse forcefully and release the ball once toward the target.
execution.endpoint: One repetition ends when the ball leaves both hands toward the target.
execution.returnPhase: Retrieve the ball or receive it after the repetition, then reset tall on both knees before the next throw.
execution.controlledJoints: Rotate without sitting back, lifting either knee, or arching through the low back.
execution.supportAndPosture: Stay upright on both knees and shins and keep the receiving area clear.
disqualifyingCompensations: Planting one foot changes the exercise into half-kneeling.
Sitting toward the heels removes the tall-kneeling support.
Slamming into the floor changes the target and family.
execution.sideOrDirection: Complete the set toward one side, then turn around and perform equal repetitions in the other direction.
